record.paper_title: Non-Supersymmetric (but) Extreme Black Holes, Scalar Hair and Other Open Problems
record.context_brief: Quantum-state interpretation of Schwarzschild in supergravity
record.original_question: Can a classical Schwarzschild black-hole solution in N = 1, d = 4 supergravity be consistently associated with a quantum state so that the positivity/Bogomol'nyi bound M ≥ 0 can be derived from the quantum supergravity theory, rather than assumed through energy conditions?

evidence.quote: These bounds can be obtained via a Nester construction [3] (see also [4]) or by associating the classical solution to a state in the quantum SUGRA theory. In the first case, certain assumptions concerning boundary and energy conditions have to be made. In the second case, one first has to make sure that such a states really does exist.

The bosonic part of this theory is GR. The B bound is equivalent to the positivity of energy [3] M ≥ 0. The only static BH solution is Schwarzschild's which depends only on M and becomes Minkowski space in the M = 0 (extreme and supersymmetric) limit.

If we associate a quantum state to Schwarzschild's solution11 (or assume some energy conditions) M will always be positive and the solution with M < 0 which has naked singularities will be excluded from the theory.
It is not clear that this can be done.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider N = 1, four-dimensional supergravity, whose bosonic sector coincides with pure Einstein gravity. The only static, asymptotically flat, spherically symmetric black-hole solution of the bosonic equations of motion is the Schwarzschild solution, parametrized by a single real mass parameter M ∈ ℝ; for M > 0 it describes a black hole, for M = 0 it reduces to Minkowski space, and for M < 0 it contains a naked singularity. The Bogomol'nyi/positivity bound in this theory asserts M ≥ 0. One way to derive this bound is by a Nester-type spinorial construction, which requires imposing suitable asymptotic boundary conditions and dominant-energy-type conditions. An alternative route is to associate the classical Schwarzschild solution with a genuine quantum state |ψ_M⟩ in the Hilbert space of quantum N = 1, d = 4 supergravity, such that ⟨ψ_M|Ĥ|ψ_M⟩ = M, and to derive M ≥ 0 directly from the positivity of the supercharge algebra {Q, Q†} ≥ 0 acting on this state.

Problem: Establish whether, within N = 1, d = 4 supergravity, the classical Schwarzschild black-hole solution can be consistently identified with such a quantum state of the quantum supergravity theory in a way that yields the positivity bound M ≥ 0 as a consequence of the quantum theory itself (in particular, of the supersymmetry algebra), without invoking classical energy or boundary conditions. Equivalently, prove or disprove the existence of a quantum supergravity state corresponding to the Schwarzschild geometry from which M ≥ 0 follows by quantum-mechanical positivity arguments.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of associating a non-supersymmetric Schwarzschild geometry with a concrete state in quantum N=1 d=4 supergravity, and deriving M ≥ 0 from the quantum theory rather than from classical energy conditions, does not appear to have been resolved in the literature; standard derivations of the positivity bound continue to rely on Nester-type spinorial constructions with classical energy/boundary assumptions. No definitive construction or no-go result for such a quantum-state identification was located.

status_evidence.title: Positive energy theorem (Witten/Nester construction)
status_evidence.snippet: Proofs via spinorial Nester-Witten methods rely on asymptotic and energy conditions to establish M ≥ 0.
status_evidence.claim: The standard derivation of the positivity bound in supergravity uses classical energy/boundary conditions, not a quantum-state identification.
